title: Home on the Range
origin: Words by Brewster M. Higley, 'My Western Home' (1873); music by Daniel E. Kelley (1873); first verse only

title: Joy to the World
origin: Words Isaac Watts (1719); tune arranged by Lowell Mason (1839)

title: My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean
origin: Scottish folk song, published by H. J. Fuller (Charles E. Pratt) in 1881; first verse and chorus

title: Oh My Darling, Clementine
origin: American western folk ballad, published by Percy Montrose (1884); first verse and chorus only

title: Simple Gifts
origin: Shaker song by Joseph Brackett (1848); first half of the verse (the second half begins 'When true simplicity is gained')

title: Angels We Have Heard on High
origin: French carol 'Les Anges dans nos campagnes' (18th century); English words James Chadwick (1862); first verse and refrain
publicDomainBasis: Traditional tune; English words published 1862 (Chadwick d.1882)

title: Can-Can
origin: Jacques Offenbach, 'Galop infernal' from Orpheus in the Underworld (1858); simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Published 1858; Offenbach died 1880; English words written in-house

title: Deck the Halls
origin: Welsh carol tune 'Nos Galan' (16th century); English words by Thomas Oliphant (1862)

title: Fur Elise
origin: Ludwig van Beethoven, Bagatelle in A minor WoO 59 'Fur Elise' (composed 1810, published 1867), opening theme; simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Published 1867; Beethoven died 1827; English words written in-house

title: Greensleeves
origin: Traditional English tune, registered 1580; instrumental theme

title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
origin: Words by Charles Wesley (1739, altered by George Whitefield 1753); music by Felix Mendelssohn (Festgesang, 1840), adapted by William H. Cummings (1855)
publicDomainBasis: Published 1739 and 1840/1855; Wesley died 1788, Mendelssohn died 1847, Cummings died 1915

title: In the Hall of the Mountain King
origin: Edvard Grieg, 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' from Peer Gynt (1875), main theme in A minor; simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Published 1875-88; Grieg died 1907; English words written in-house

title: Minuet in G
origin: Christian Petzold, Minuet in G major BWV Anh. 114, from the Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725); simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Written 1725; Petzold died 1733; English words written in-house

title: Polly Wolly Doodle
origin: American song printed in Students' Songs (Harvard, 1880); first verse and chorus in standard spelling

title: Rondo alla Turca (Turkish March)
origin: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Piano Sonata No. 11 in A major K. 331, third movement (published 1784); opening theme, sixteenths written as eighths, instrumental (phrase labels, no words)

title: Silent Night
origin: Franz Xaver Gruber, words Joseph Mohr (1818); English words John Freeman Young (1859); first verse only
publicDomainBasis: Published 1818/1859; Gruber d.1863, Mohr d.1848, Young d.1885

title: The Blue Danube Waltz
origin: Johann Strauss II, 'An der schönen blauen Donau' Op. 314 (1867); main waltz theme, instrumental (phrase labels, no words)

title: Toreador March
origin: Georges Bizet, Toreador Song (Couplets) from the opera Carmen (1875); verse theme as an instrumental

title: Turkey in the Straw
origin: American fiddle tune, published as 'Turkey in de Straw' (1861) from the earlier minstrel song 'Zip Coon' (1834); instrumental (phrase labels, no words)

title: Yankee Doodle
origin: Anglo-American song from the 1760s-1770s
